how: A fresh session loads the skill. Case ft-00 (derive): given the character below, derive the test; the derived question must name the same trait (wording may differ). Cases ft-01 to ft-08 (apply): apply the stated test to the line; compare pass/fail. ft-09 (scope) and ft-10, ft-11 (failure modes at review) check what the skill says, not a pass/fail on a line. Record the run in runs.md.
character: The Quiet Refuser: restraint, presence, considered confidence. Refuses the hospitality default of effusive welcome. Vocabulary: plain, quiet, real.
test: Is this effusive? (markers: exclamation marks, self-praise of the venue, performed warmth)

cases.rule: Derive: one dominant trait, usually a refusal, phrased in the brand's own vocabulary with markers

cases.line: Welcome to our wonderful restaurant! We're so excited to have you here this evening!!
Lamb shoulder, slow-cooked, served with the broth.
Our master chef's signature lamb, lovingly hand-prepared over twelve hours.
Tomorrow's lamb is delayed by a day. We'll run the duck through Friday lunch.
Hi team, sorry to bother you but unfortunately we have a small issue with the lamb tomorrow!!
That's not yours — I'll fix it.
Oh my goodness I am SO sorry, let me make this right for you right away, anything you need!

cases.expected: out of scope: a tagline is judged by the brand book, not the filter test; the skill must say so rather than fail it
cases.rule: Scope: the name, the tagline and the lockup are judged by vios-name-and-tagline, not the filter test

cases.expected: rejected as too lenient: friendliness is a trait the whole category shares, so the question passes competitor copy; the skill names the failure mode and returns to the dominant trait (refusal of effusion)
fail_if: the failure mode is not named
cases.rule: Failure mode: too lenient (names a trait the category shares)

cases.proposed_question: Does this contain an exclamation mark?
cases.expected: rejected as too strict: it tests a mark, not the trait, so 'Our master chef's signature lamb, lovingly hand-prepared' would pass; the skill names the failure mode and keeps the exclamation mark as one marker under the trait question
fail_if: ft-04 would pass under it and the skill does not say so
cases.rule: Failure mode: too strict (tests a word, not the trait)
